channel.description: Recent content in Teaching on Adolfo De Unánue

item.title: Ciencia para futuros tomadores de decisión
item.description: Energy, warming, health, logistics, quantum computing: the political and economic questions increasingly turn on technical content, and a leader who misreads the science will decide badly. The concepts and techniques that help someone decide, for people who already make decisions and people who are about to.

item.title: Ciencia de Datos para Políticas Públicas
item.description: Turning analysis into action, and deliberately not a course on machine-learning methods. Built on Rayid Ghani and Kit Rodolfa’s Machine Learning in Practice at Carnegie Mellon, which itself comes out of the Data Science for Social Good fellowship.

item.title: State-Guided Optimization: The Chinese Approach
item.description: Operations research for national infrastructure networks, taught through the way one state directs them. Twelve weeks organised around the claim that an objective function is a political statement about who is served first — the same argument the rest of this site makes, worked out at the length a course allows.

item.title: Systems concepts for public policy
item.description: Systems thinking, complex adaptive systems and systems engineering put to societal problems — past the linear and reductionist habit, toward interdisciplinary and systemic policy.

item.title: Inspecciones
item.description: The state must verify that people and firms comply with far more rules than it can ever inspect, so the real question is which inspections to run. A course on prioritising scarce enforcement capacity.
